capabilities: mark tasks with custom status characters via a modal, hotkey or right-click menu
cycle task marks forward and backward through a configured sequence
collect tasks of a group under a configured area heading
append formatted timestamps and remove old appended text when marking
expose an API other plugins can use to check whether a mark means complete
disambiguation: Not just a completed-task archiver; its main job is changing task status marks, with collection as an optional feature.
extras: Detailed configuration reference (menus and modals, task collection) lives in a separate docs/README.md rather than the main README.
intentEvidence: Yet another plugin to manage completed tasks, but this one has a task-completion modal to go with it!
motivation: The author explains choosing the word 'mark' because it covers both the symbol and the action of marking, and notes 'Naming things is hard.'
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to set arbitrary task status marks or regroup completed tasks within a note from a quick pop-up.

relations.evidence: Completed Area Plugin -- general premise of moving completed tasks to a different area within the note

summary: Task mark plugin that changes task status via a modal, hotkeys or context menus, and can collect completed tasks under a heading.
